rationale.conceptual: The paper presents a custom extension of the loop algorithm tailored to models with biquadratic interactions. It involves an iterative method to determine a projection axis, careful handling of detailed balance, and multiple interacting components (lattice geometry, Hamiltonian, coloring, loop construction, three flip variants). Translating the method to code correctly requires non-trivial understanding of the algorithm and subtle implementation choices.
rationale.execution: The implementation is a single script that performs lattice setup, MC simulation with both single-spin and loop updates, and records acceptance rates. The pipeline is straightforward: no complex tooling, no multi-stage orchestration, only standard libraries (numpy) and file output. There are a few sub-steps, but they are sequential within one codebase.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a non-trivial extended loop algorithm for a classical Heisenberg model with biquadratic interactions, including on-the-fly determination of a common axis, loop construction, and three distinct flip methods. The underlying physics and algorithmic details demand genuine understanding and careful coding. The pipeline is essentially a single MC simulation script with modest I/O, and resource requirements are minimal (CPU-only, tiny memory).
